dedupe_keys.name: high resolution layer tree cover and forests copernicus

description: The High Resolution Layer Tree Cover and Forests is a pan-European raster product of the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service, run for the European Union by the European Environment Agency (EEA). It maps tree cover density on a continuous 1 to 100 percent scale as far as detectable from 10 m satellite imagery, the dominant leaf type (broadleaved or coniferous), and a forest type layer following the FAO forest definition. Tree cover density and dominant leaf type are updated annually and available from 2018 to 2021, forest type every three years, and all products also exist for the 2012 and 2015 reference years; auxiliary layers can be requested from the service desk, and the 2018 leaf type products were replaced by new versions covering the EEA38 countries. Rasters are downloaded from the CLMS portal under the Copernicus data policy of free, full and open access. Caveats: the classification is a remote sensing product with omission and commission errors near urban edges, the replaced 2018 versions and the UK coverage differ, and 10 m pixels do not resolve single street trees. The layers serve urban and peri-urban green infrastructure mapping, vegetation management near power lines and railways, wildfire and heat exposure analysis and climate adaptation studies, and complement the Urban Atlas Street Tree Layer catalogued here.
